Subject: Combined HIPAA + FERPA addenda request for pilot

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for the quick intro last week — excited to explore Redwood for our school-based health pilot. We run health clinics inside several K-12 districts and will be processing both student education records and protected health information. Procurement asked me to kick off a combined feasibility check: can Redwood support a single addendum (or set of paired addenda) that covers HIPAA (BAA) requirements and FERPA concerns for student PII?

High-level ask:
- Feasibility of signing a BAA + FERPA/education-data addendum for the pilot
- Any residency/responsibility constraints for student PHI/Education data (we are US-based, some districts require onshore processing)
- Subprocessor list and whether you can blacklist certain infra providers for this engagement
- Timeline for a first-draft addendum and an estimate for SOC2 / security artifacts we should expect to receive for procurement

I've attached a short request summary (CareLearn_DPA_Request.pdf) that shows the workflows and sample schema. Our procurement contact is procurement@carelearn.com — cc'd here for visibility.

Goal: start pilot pilot onboarding in ~60 days if feasible.

Thanks,

Emma — thanks for the clear summary and the attachment. We're positioned to support regulated workloads, and we can propose a modular approach so you get a single source-of-truth addenda bundle that covers BAA language plus FERPA/education-specific clauses. A few quick clarifying questions before Vanessa drafts the legal outline:

1) Scope of data types: the sample schema helps, but can you confirm whether the pilot will include any image uploads (scanned intake forms) or only structured text/fields?
2) Residency: is US-only processing a hard requirement for the pilot? If some districts require specific states, please flag which ones.
3) Subprocessor restrictions: do you have any absolute blacklist (e.g., no multi-tenant caches, no specific cloud regions/providers)?
4) Required artifacts: procurement asked for SOC2 Type II, encryption attestation, and an expected list of subprocessors — anything else they need for their vendor assessment?

We'll produce a proposed addenda outline and a draft in the next 5 business days. Vanessa, Marcus — looping you in to confirm legal and technical gating items. Karthik, I'll keep you posted on timelines for SOW/pricing.

Best,

Emma / Soojin — thanks for pulling this together. I've reviewed the request doc and sketched an approach:

- We'll deliver a modular addenda package: (A) Base DPA (data processing + standard security), (B) HIPAA BAA annex, (C) FERPA annex with student-data-specific definitions and parental-consent language where applicable. Each annex will call out residual liability, audit rights, and breach notification timelines.
- For residency, Redwood supports US-only operations and can commit to region scoping on a per-deal basis (we'll put specific states in the exhibit if required).
- Subprocessors: we publish a current list and will provide an export. We can consider blacklist requests but may require migration to Dedicated/Private deployment if a critical subprocessor must be removed.
- Deliverables & timeline (provisional):
  * Day 0: Receive confirmed data types + residency constraints from CareLearn
  * Day 3: Redwood legal delivers addenda outline (attached)
  * Day 14: Redwood provides first draft addenda for procurement review
  * Day 28: Target for signed addenda assuming typical redline cycle (may extend if substantial legal procurement negotiation)

Required outs from CareLearn: the procurement POC, a prioritized list of required compliance artifacts (SOC2, encryption attestations, PCI if relevant), and any absolute subprocessors blacklist.

I've attached the proposed outline to this message (proposed_addenda_outline.pdf). I'll prepare a first-draft addenda (word doc) once we have the confirmed scope.

Regards,

Emma / team — quick technical gating notes from security/infra:

- Data types: if the pilot includes images/scans we need to know expected retention and whether PII will be OCR-processed. OCR pipelines may affect where we place caching and persistent storage.
- Residency: US-only processing is supported. If any districts require a specific state residency, we recommend Dedicated capacity pinned to that region.
- Key management: we can support customer-managed keys (KMS) for Dedicated/Private deployments; hosted customers typically use Redwood-managed keys but we can present attestations.
- Subprocessors: current infra subprocessors include AWS (us-west-2, us-east-1), CloudCacheInc, and a managed logging provider. If CareLearn requires removal of CloudCacheInc, migration to a Dedicated pool is likely.
- Audit and logs: we can provide token-level request logs, per-request latency/cost traces, and redacted payload logs for audit. For SOC2 evidence, we can package the standard artifact bundle.
- Suggested minimum for pilot security SLOs: encrypted at rest (AES-256), TLS1.2+ in transit, 30-day access logging retention (extendable), and monthly vulnerability scans for Dedicated.

If you can share the sample schema (thanks for the csv) and an estimated daily message volume, I can map an infra recommendation (hosted vs dedicated) and call out where redwood can make contractual commitments.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Security Engineering, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Thanks everyone — this is super helpful. Short answers:
- Data types: structured intake fields + occasional scanned consent forms (PDFs). We do plan to OCR consent forms.
- Residency: US-only is mandatory for the pilot; no state-level restrictions at onboarding, but a few districts may later require specific state residency (we'll flag those during rollout).
- Blacklist: CareLearn cannot work with CloudCacheInc per district rules.
- Artifacts: Procurement asked for SOC2 Type II, encryption attestation, subprocessors list, and last 12 months of uptime incidents (summary).
- Estimated volume: 8k messages/day across pilot districts (peak), small file uploads ~200/day.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood produces the first-draft addenda & an infra recommendation (hosted vs dedicated) based on the above scope
2) Karthik / Redwood sales to send a high-level SOW + pricing option for a 60-day pilot (incl. pricing delta for Dedicated if required)
3) Procurement to receive artifacts (SOC2, attestations) and start internal review

Procurement is copied on this thread and will expect the deliverables above. Thanks — we can jump on a quick call if helpful.

Best,
